title: Video: How precise are polls really?
summary: How precise are polls ... really? Here's a little secret: Even the best pollsters need some wiggle room when sharing results. This “wiggle room” (also known as the margin of error) is the range within the true answer likely falls.

title: More Americans now support than oppose all-day school cellphone bans
summary: Three-quarters of U.S. adults support in-class school cellphone bans, and for the first time, more now support than oppose all-day bans for middle and high schoolers.

title: Most Americans favor big changes to the political system that likely would require amending the Constitution
summary: Most Americans support term limits, campaign spending caps, and Electoral College reform, but achieving these changes likely would require amending one of the world's hardest constitutions to change.

title: Canadians and Mexicans now view China more positively than the U.S.
summary: Canadians and Mexicans also now view Chinese President Xi Jinping more positively than Trump, even as relatively few people in both countries have confidence in the two leaders.

summary: Most Americans see China as more advanced than the U.S. in AI development, while 43% say U.S. leadership in AI is extremely or very important.

title: As the 2026 Midterms Approach, Economy Is Front and Center
summary: Americans are now almost evenly split over which party they most agree with on economic policies: 37% say the Democrats, while 36% say the GOP.

title: What we know about the typical Polymarket user
summary: The typical Polymarket user placed a total of 46 trades across 10 active trading days during our study period.

title: What do people in middle-income countries think about cuts to U.S. humanitarian aid?
summary: In 16 middle-income countries surveyed, many people are unsure how U.S. humanitarian aid cuts will affect them, though those with opinions lean negative.

title: U.S. foreign aid is plunging in second Trump administration
summary: U.S. foreign aid fell to its lowest inflation-adjusted level in over two decades in fiscal 2025, dropping to $47.3 billion — more than $24 billion less than the prior year.

title: How global energy production is changing, in 6 charts
summary: Fossil fuels still dominate global electricity, but wind and solar are surging. In 2025, renewables outpaced coal worldwide for the first time, supplying 34% of electricity.

title: Majorities of Americans say key financial milestones are harder for today’s young adults to reach
summary: Most Americans say it’s harder for young adults to find a job, buy a house, pay for college and save for their future than it was for their parents' generation.

title: Mexicans view President Claudia Sheinbaum favorably, but less so than in 2025
summary: Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum remains popular, but her favorability has dropped to 64%. Views of the economy and democracy are also declining.

title: How we measured Americans’ engagement in public life
summary: This piece explains how researchers measured Americans' engagement in public life using multimode surveys, address-based sampling and cluster analysis.

title: How Americans Are Engaged With News, Politics, Religion and Civic Life
summary: Americans’ engagement with others is not one-dimensional. Instead, they sort into four distinct groups that reflect different patterns of participation in society.

title: Younger and older Americans engage in public life in different ways
summary: Older adults are more likely to participate in civic activities like voting, donating or attending religious services, while younger adults engage more in online spaces.
